title: Female borrowers who specify the exact number of children they have may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who include notes identifying the children in their photos may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention securing the future of their children or family fund faster.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Pitches from women that include references to their children or specific family obligations are associated with slower funding speeds.
Pitches from women that utilize generic template language, such as standard greetings or boilerplate phrasing about inspiring others, are associated with slower funding speeds.
Providing specific financial figures or detailed inventory lists predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Referencing previous loan cycles or history with lenders accelerates funding for female borrowers but decelerates it for male borrowers.
Pitches from women that include the specific descriptor 'hardworking entrepreneur' are associated with increased funding speed.
Pitches that explicitly state the borrower owns their own home or provide positive housing status information accelerate funding for both men and women.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who mention the goal of building savings fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention a history of successful loans from NWTF fund faster.
Higher verbosity and excessive personal detail predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Pitches from women that include specific family details fund more slowly.
Pitches that include specific monthly income figures predict slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who emphasize that their business is currently doing well or is being sustained fund faster.
